semantic._note: Generation four — the Lovable design handoff's theme.css (packages/brand/lovable-handoff), received 28 September 2026 and decided by the Founder that day: its look wins every visual question. Nineteen semantic roles, each with a light and a dark value. The handoff writes most of them in oklch; each is stored here as the sRGB hex it converts to exactly (OKLab → linear sRGB → gamma, rounded to eight bits — Chromium's canvas paints the same eight values) with the oklch string kept beside it for the CI document, and a colour the handoff wrote as a hex literal is kept as that literal. The names are dotted where the rest of the build reads them — light.primary, dark.surface — because three of them (surface, danger, info) collide with current-generation names screens still read: a refusal label painted with the earlier danger must go on clearing 4.5:1 until the screen that paints it is restyled, so the new generation gets its own address rather than overwriting the old one's. On the web they arrive as --color-<name>, which is the name the handoff's own @theme block gives them; natively as ThusoSemantic.Light / ThusoSemantic.Dark.
semantic._darkNote: The dark values exist so the variables exist. No screen is restyled for dark in this generation's first wave; the web emits them under prefers-color-scheme: dark, guarded so data-theme="light" on :root wins, and under :root[data-theme="dark"]. Nothing reads them yet.

accentForeground.gamut: a hair outside sRGB; clipped per channel to the nearest displayable value, which is what every sRGB screen paints for it

radius_note: The handoff's three radii — sm 6, md 8, lg 12 — since 28 September 2026, and the five names the product already spends mapped onto them: card and panel are lg, control and tile are md, pill stays 999. The mapping is enforced by scripts/check-boundaries.mjs, so the whole product took compact corners in one change and cannot drift back a card at a time. They were 20 / 28 / 16 / 16 before.
elevation_note: The handoff's --shadow-sm and --shadow-md, since 28 September 2026: 0 1px 2px oklch(0.24 0.052 239 / 0.06) and 0 8px 24px oklch(0.24 0.052 239 / 0.1). Written here as rgba of the same colour — oklch(0.24 0.052 239) is light.foreground, #022235 — because that is the form the stylesheets already spend as --shadow and --shadow-raised. card is the handoff's sm and raised is its md; there is no third.

families.text: Figtree (variable, self-hosted on the web at weights 400–800, latin and latin-ext; system-ui on iOS and Android this wave)
families.display: Outfit (variable, self-hosted on the web at weights 500–700, latin and latin-ext; system-ui on iOS and Android this wave). There is a second face again, on purpose. The note that used to sit here said Inter did everything because a decorative serif across a clinical product's headlines read as an editorial about health; that was true of the serif, and it is not an argument against a second sans. The Lovable handoff of 28 September 2026 sets Outfit for page titles and compact feature headings and Figtree for everything a person has to read carefully, and the Founder decided that day that the handoff's look wins. Inter's two woff2 files and its licence stay in apps/web/public/fonts for now, referenced by nothing; a later wave removes them.
families.note: The handoff states no type sizes, so the scale below is unchanged.

typography.minimumRenderedNote: The floor tests/accessibility.spec.ts enforces on rendered text. It used to be 11 while the same file called 13 the minimum for body text — a two-point gap that unread counts, chart axes and tab-bar labels lived in. The gap is closed rather than described: the caption size is now 13 and the floor is the caption size, so the two agree. That is a type-scale decision with a layout consequence on every dense screen, and the layouts were changed to take it rather than the number being nudged to fit them.
typography.scaleNote: Six steps became seven. Both native passes stopped at the same gap: sectionTitle is 18 and screenTitle is 28, and a card that leads a screen wants something between them — every one of them had reached for 22 and typed it. A step nobody can find is a step everybody invents.
typography.metricNote: Two steps, because a metric is the design's signature and it is read at two distances. `metric` (32) is a figure in a row of them; `metricLarge` (40) is the one figure a screen leads with, and the web takes it above 900px. They were 32 on iOS and 40-then-42 on the web with only 32 declared, which meant the shape the whole language is built around was a different size on two platforms and nothing said which was right.

targets.why: A control smaller than a fingertip is not a smaller control, it is a control somebody misses while standing in a doorway holding a child. WCAG 2.2 puts the AA floor at 24x24 (SC 2.5.8) and the AAA figure at 44x44 (SC 2.5.5); this design is held to 44 because it is a health app operated one-handed, and everything that is not is listed below with what it measures instead. tests/accessibility.spec.ts reads this list, so an exemption is a line in the contract rather than a line in a test.
targets.exemptions: A link inside a running paragraph, and an input the design hides behind its own label — the label is the target and is measured in its place.

knownUndersized.note: Twenty-four square, the AA floor, and every slide it selects is also reachable from the pause control and by letting the carousel run. Making it 44 would space three dots across 132px and turn a quiet indicator into the loudest thing on the banner.

An inline text action inside a dense row — a provenance note, a call roster line. At 44 it would double the height of every row it sits in. Every one of them has a full-size equivalent elsewhere on the screen.
Only undersized where it is not a button. Where it is one — the profile control in the top bar — it is 44.

motion._note: One curve and three durations, so everything in the product accelerates the same way. They were written into apps/web/src/surface/glass.css and stopped there, which made them a second motion system alongside durationMs above — reachable by the web and by nothing else, so a spring on iOS and a tween on Android were each somebody's private guess at what the web was doing. easeSoft is a cubic bezier's two control points; it overshoots very slightly at the end, which is what reads as smooth rather than linear. quick is a press or a colour change, settle is a control coming to rest, enter is something arriving on screen for the first time. durationMs is older and narrower — the single duration the native theme layers already spend — and is kept because retiring it is a separate change from giving the other two platforms the curve.
motion._reducedMotionNote: respectReducedMotion is not a suggestion and not a speed setting. Reduced motion REMOVES these animations rather than shortening them: a 420ms entrance run at 80ms is still a thing that moved. Web answers prefers-reduced-motion, iOS answers accessibilityReduceMotion, and Android follows the system animator duration scale — which reports 0 when a reader has turned animations off, so a duration multiplied by it is genuinely none.

contrast.why: A palette is either measured or it is a matter of opinion, and colour is the one part of a design where an opinion held by somebody with ordinary eyesight is worth nothing to the reader who cannot use the result. Every foreground and background this design actually puts together is listed below with the ratio it has to clear, and scripts/check-boundaries.mjs computes each one from the hexes above on every build. A pair that is not listed is a pair nobody has checked, which is why adding a colour combination to the design means adding a row here first. Vital Teal and Mango appear here only against the 3:1 non-text floor: at 2.49:1 and 1.78:1 on white they are brand marks, not labels, and the two ink variants beside them are what carries the words.
contrast.standard: WCAG 2.2 AA. 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text (18.66px bold or 24px and over) and for the visual boundary of a control or a focus indicator (SC 1.4.11). The focus indicator is two rings, not one: no single colour clears 3:1 against both a white card and a forest panel, and controls exist on both. A light inner ring carries the dark grounds and a dark outer ring carries the light ones, so whichever ground it lands on, one of the two is legible. Tying the ring to --amber, which also labels warnings, made the two pull against each other the moment the warning was darkened enough to be readable.

contrast.sageNote: Sage is a fill and never a label. The darkest of the four measures 2.54:1 as text on mist, which clears nothing — the same rule teal and mango are held to. Everything a reader must actually read is charcoal, which clears 5.89:1 on even the darkest sage in the ramp, so the ramp stops at sageSlate: one step further and charcoal stops carrying. This bit once: a lead panel painted sage and a heading rule set faint on a child of it, and nothing computed the pair because the ground and the colour were set by two different rules — the failure existed only where they met. Both the stylesheet and the Android theme now provide charcoal from the surface that paints the sage, so a child cannot get it wrong by forgetting.
contrast.faintNote: faint was #5D6B80 and passed on white and mist by luck rather than by construction: it measured 4.30 on cloud, and cloud is what a recessed panel becomes in the new surface system. The pair was declared nowhere, so the build was silent rather than red — and the token is used 180 times in the web stylesheet, so the sweep moving panels onto cloud would have turned a great many of those into failures nothing reported. It is #59677B now, four per cent darker at the same hue, which clears every neutral ground in the palette: 5.05 on mist, 4.57 on cloud, 5.75 on surface, 5.25 on canvas. All four are declared above so the build holds them rather than the absence of a declaration keeping them quiet. It was not exempted: knownFailures was emptied earlier and an exemption is not the answer to a colour that can simply be corrected.
contrast.lovableNote: Generation four's rows, added 28 September 2026: every foreground the handoff's theme.css defines against every surface it defines, light and dark, dotted as light.<role> / dark.<role> and resolved from #semantic. 90 clear their floor and 34 do not and are parked below with a measured replacement each. The pattern in the failures is the handoff's own: on a light ground its accent, success, info and ring (#189870) clear only the 3:1 non-text floor, and its danger, coral, warning and highlight — brand orange and brand lime — clear nothing at all, so on a light screen those four are fills and marks and never words, and white text on the orange fails too. On a dark ground every one of them clears text. The two that fail in the dark are primary as text on a raised or muted panel and light text on an orange or lime fill.

color_sourceNote: mist, cloud, stone, charcoal and the four sages are the published palette of the Nura healthcare dashboard, which the founder chose as the visual direction on 8 September 2026. They are surface colours and one near-black; they replace no semantic colour. danger, info, focus and the clinical accents keep their own values and were re-measured against the new ground rather than assumed.

colorGenerations._note: Which colour is authoritative for what, because there are now three generations in this file and 'a number lives in one place' had quietly acquired three answers to 'what colour is a card ground'. Additive was the right call on 8 September — two agents and a second session were mid-flight and a rename would have lost work — but additive without a record is how a palette becomes sediment. This is the record, and check-boundaries.mjs fails a colour that is in neither list, so a thirty-fifth token is a decision rather than a drift.
colorGenerations.retirementNote: The indigo, teal and mango ramps are not superseded and are not going: they are the funding proposal's own brand and they carry meaning the sage ramp cannot — a refusal, a warning, a value in range. What is superseded is only the two neutrals the new ground replaces. The retirement pass belongs with the surface sweep, once the entry split and the capability sweep have landed, and it is one commit: repoint canvas and ink at their successors, then delete them. Not before — a rename during surgery is how the last collision happened.
colorGenerations.generationFourNote: The fourth generation, 28 September 2026, is #semantic, not a set of names in color: its nineteen roles each carry a light and a dark value, and they are named light.<role> and dark.<role> wherever this file or a check points at one. It supersedes the indigo ramp, the ten studio colours, the four sages, the three auroras and glow — each pointed above at the role that takes its place. mist, cloud, stone and charcoal stay current because they are the ground every screen still stands on until it is restyled; teal, tealInk and the mango ramp stay current because they carry a refusal, a warning and a value in range, which the handoff's warning (brand lime) cannot carry as text on a light ground; brandMint stays because the handoff does not mention it and the clinical deck reads it. Retirement, as before, is one commit that repoints and deletes, after the screens have moved.

glass._note: Frosted panels, and the one discipline that makes them safe. A translucent surface has no fixed colour — it is whatever is behind it, tinted — so a contrast figure measured against it is a guess about position. Every glass surface in this product therefore declares a FLOOR: the composite of its tint over the darkest point any ground reaches. Contrast is measured against the floor, which is a real colour, and the build refuses a glass surface that does not declare one. That is the whole reason this can be done in a product that computes contrast on every build.
glass.edgeNote: A one-pixel highlight along the top edge at 60% white is what makes a frosted panel read as glass rather than as a pale card. It carries no text and is not measured.
glass.fallbackNote: backdrop-filter is expensive on the mid-range Android handsets this product is actually for. Where it is unsupported — and inside @media (prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce) — glass resolves to the opaque floor colour, which is exactly the colour every contrast figure was measured against. The fallback is not a degradation; it is the measured case.
glass.neverOnText: A glass panel may not sit on top of text. Blur behind a word is the one place translucency stops being decoration and starts being a legibility problem.

opacity._note: Secondary text on a surface is charcoal at 72%, not a grey. Both native agents arrived at the same value independently — iOS was drawing charcoal.opacity(0.72) in about twenty-five places — and both asked for a token, which is the signal it should be one. It is an alpha rather than a hex on purpose: flattened over white it is #5C5C5C, which measures 4.36 on paleSage and 3.51 on softSage and fails both. As an opacity it composites with whatever it sits on and darkens as the ground does — 6.69 on white, 6.01 on cloud, 5.37 on paleSage, 4.74 on softSage. A fixed grey cannot follow its ground; an alpha has no choice but to.

color_studioNote: September 2026 editorial direction: warm paper, botanical ink and pale citron for care, with a muted lavender journal. The original brand palette is separate and is not recoloured. Decorative fills carry dark text; studioLime is permitted as text only on the declared dark ground. All supported foreground/background pairs are calculated by check-boundaries.mjs; numerical contrast claims belong to that calculation rather than prose.
color_brandNote: Since 28 September 2026 the brand values are the Lovable handoff's exact literals — brandInk #083848, brandGreen #189870, brandOrange #F86830, brandLime #D8F818 — decided by the Founder that day; the 23 September values (#0F3B4A, #1D9E75, #FF6B35, #D9FF1A) are superseded, and brandMint #9FE1CB is unchanged because the handoff does not carry a mint. The official logos are the handoff's own PNG masters under packages/brand/lovable-handoff and are never redrawn or recoloured; the SVG cuts under apps/web/public/brand were drawn from the 23 September values and are a separate question for a later wave. Brand orange and lime are decorative on light surfaces. Consult the computed contrast pairs for permitted text uses.
color_lovableNote: Generation four: the Lovable design handoff, received 28 September 2026, decided by the Founder on 28 September 2026 — the handoff's look wins every visual question; the build's logic, contracts and refusals win everything else. What it brought: the nineteen semantic roles in #semantic, light and dark; the four brand literals above; the three radii and two shadows; Outfit for display and Figtree for text. What it did not change: spacing stays the 8-point rhythm, the type scale stays, the two native apps keep system fonts this wave, and no screen is restyled for dark. The masters are byte-identical copies under packages/brand/lovable-handoff, held to a manifest of hashes.
